description: BAFU reports metal emissions as the element and the openLCA LCIA package as the ion, so BAFU's `Mercury` lands on `Mercury` and the package's `Mercury II` on `Mercury(2+)`, and the lookup answer said nothing about the other (#379). The answer now carries `counterparts`: the flows of the substance's ions, or of its element and sibling ions, in the same compartment, each with its factor count, read off the `ion_of` relation `flow_layers.ions` records on every ion substance it tied to its element. That is a property of the lookup, held by tests/test_lookup_matcher.py; what a build can be asked is that the two flows the page's example names exist, one each.

expectations.title: `Mercury(2+)` to air, unspecified is one active flow, which the other's lookup answer names as its counterpart
expectations.comment: The worked example on the lookup page: BAFU's `Mercury` lands on the metal and openLCA's `Mercury II` on the ion, and each answer's `counterparts` names the other flow in this compartment, read off the `ion_of` relation the ions layer records on `Mercury(2+)`. Held so the example stays a flow that exists; on the build of 21 October 2026 (commit 931ed30) it was 653d74e8-d259-4d3d-81b3-4f47c391fd51 with 6 factors.
